daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) conducted a sting operation at BNPB, the national disaster management agency, with the operation related to procurement of goods and services. BNPB has secured documents and launched an internal investigation following the sting, while reminding the public of the presumption of innocence. The incident adds to what observers describe as a crisis of integrity in public institutions.

  • An analysis found that two years into the Prabowo administration, political consolidation has advanced faster than technocratic governance.
  • Police Chief Suyudi issued another rotation telegram affecting 12 high-ranking police officers.
  • The Air Force Chief reshuffled 11 strategic positions in the TNI AU, including the appointment of Air Marshal Ian Fuady as Air Operations Commander.
  • Golkar responded to a Celios survey critical of minister Bahlil by suggesting a political conspiracy.
  • The term of office for regional legislatures (DPRD) elected in 2024 has been challenged at the Constitutional Court with a request to extend it to 2031.
  • An opinion piece questioned who benefits from the DPR's selective access policies.
  • A commentary examined the DPR's constitutional responsibilities regarding Vice President Gibran's academic credentials.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Israel forced an Ethiopian Airlines flight to turn back because its pilot was Indonesian, marking an unusual aviation incident with diplomatic implications. Meanwhile, Indonesia's defense modernization continues as the country marks two years of the Prabowo-Gibran administration, with military modernization proceeding amid strategic defense challenges.

  • The Indonesian embassy in Yaoundé is targeting US$19.5 million in transactions at TEI 2026.
  • Indonesia urged UNESCO to protect culture amid AI and climate risks.
  • Vice President Gibran stated that tourism is one of Indonesia's soft power instruments.

Other

President Prabowo issued multiple directives on forest fire management as the crisis intensifies across Kalimantan and Sumatra. The government aims to extinguish the fires within a month, while water and fuel shortages hamper firefighting efforts in South Kalimantan. The worsening haze has forced Pekanbaru to implement two days of remote learning, and the government has been urged to prepare health services for the expanding smoke impact.

  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs formally opened a double-degree program in cooperation with Al-Azhar.
  • The head of a travel agency admitted to charging US$102,000 in fees to expedite hajj pilgrimages for 34 participants, with the testimony exposing corrupt practices in managing additional hajj quotas.
  • Indonesia's national team to support data center development is being planned, while a data center for digital connectivity opened in Lamongan.
  • The government vowed not to raise subsidized fuel prices despite surging oil costs.
  • BPOM partnered with 187 universities to boost the ATMP ecosystem.
